args: S="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/librarian_agent/src/mcp_server.py"; for c in python3 python py; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; "$c" -c "import mcp, jsonschema, referencing" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; exec "$c" "$S" --serve; done; if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 && uv run --offline --no-project --python 3.12 --with "mcp>=2.0" --with jsonschema python -c "import mcp, jsonschema, referencing" >/dev/null 2>&1; then exec uv run --offline --no-project --python 3.12 --with "mcp>=2.0" --with jsonschema python "$S" --serve; fi; echo "librarian: no python on PATH imports mcp, jsonschema and referencing, and uv cannot supply them offline" >&2; exit 1
librarian.$comment: git is on PATH wherever this repository was cloned; sh is NOT, and this said it was until 2026-09-24. Git for Windows installs sh.exe under Git/bin and Git/usr/bin and puts only Git/cmd on PATH. Hooks never noticed, because the harness runs them inside Git Bash, which has sh; an MCP server is spawned directly as a process from the Windows PATH, so `sh` is not found and the server never starts. `bash` is no substitute: on the Windows PATH it resolves to the WSL launcher, another App Execution Alias. On the microscope computer the remedy is machine-side -- Git/bin on the user PATH, then restart the app, since PATH is read at launch -- because no single command name is correct on every platform and a tracked file must not carry a machine path (plan.md 11-22). The interpreter is resolved by RUNNING it, not by finding it. This said until 2026-09-24 that a stock Windows install provides `python` and no `python3`, and resolved with `command -v python3 || command -v python`. On the microscope computer that is false in the way that costs most: `python3` EXISTS as a Microsoft Store App Execution Alias -- a real file on PATH that is not Python. `command -v` finds it, so the fallback never fires; it prints 'Python was not found' and exits 49, and the server never starts. That is the CONNECTION_CLOSED this session opened with. A guard that tests existence cannot tell an interpreter from a placeholder named after one, so each candidate is probed with `-c ''` and only a zero exit is accepted. PYTHONUTF8 is set because the validator and the server read repository text with no explicit encoding and Windows defaults to cp1252, which raises UnicodeDecodeError on the first non-ASCII byte (plan.md 11-22). PROBE FOR WHAT THE SERVER NEEDS, not only for a python that runs (2026-10-08, on the person's word): on the Office computer the first runnable python is Anaconda 3.9, which has no `mcp`, so the server exited at launch and no session there had the librarian's tools from 2026-10-01; every goal written there since is degraded. A candidate now counts only if it imports mcp, jsonschema and referencing; failing that, the uv form CLAUDE.md names for this computer, offline, with nothing downloaded; failing that, exit naming what is missing. Same defect and same remedy as contracts/hooks at f4f2676. Reaches only sessions started after it.
